src/data/characters.js: Daughter of the Keeper of Lanternfall. Reads every book the tide brings in. Wants, more than anything, to leave.
Wren\'s best friend since before either could walk. Herbalist\'s apprentice. Has a plan for everything, including the plan failing.
Squire of the Dawnguard, exiled to Lanternfall after he froze during his knighting trial. Loud. Kind. Certain he is a coward.
Washed ashore in a storm with no memory and a Crest no Lantern has ever seen.
Aurenne street kid. Steals for a living, lies for fun, and would die before admitting he\'s eleven.
Captain of the airship Halcyon. Smuggler, gambler, Dawnguard deserter. Owes everyone money, including himself.

s hounds, bred in the Spire\'s light. They cast no shadow at all.
An eye of noon, floating. Looking at it is like looking at the sun, which nobody has done for a year.
The Spire\'s guard. They have been promised the best day of their lives, as soon as their shift ends.
A hymn given wings. It heals whatever stands between it and you.
Keeper of the Spire\'s back door. He has turned away four hundred pilgrims and remembers every face.
Armor wound like a clock. It stops when it is struck — and so, for a moment, do you.
A moment that never ended, drifting. Cold as an afternoon that will not let you go home.
They eat memories the way other moths eat coats. The Spire is a feast.
They practice the Vespersong in shifts. Somebody, somewhere in the Spire, is always singing it.
The Spire\'s keeper of hours. It has only ever counted to twelve, and it has done so for forty years.
"Lovely day for it!" it says, and smiles, and smiles, and comes for your throat.
A festival lantern that drifted loose. The candle inside has burned for forty years and never got any shorter.
Somebody\'s dog, remembered as a very good dog. Remembered a little too hard.
"Welcome to the Festival of the Long Light. Enjoy the day." Forever.
She has been dancing round the maypole since before your parents were born. She would love you to join in.
Mercy\'s congregation. They sing for her because she promised them they would never have to stop.
Evernoon\'s warden. She believes that a day which never ends cannot hurt anyone. She has never once been told no and believed it.
Where Evernoon comes apart, the Gloam comes in. It wears whatever it finds.
Its strings are cut. Its sentence is unfinished. It is very, very angry about both.
Every sentence Evernoon never finished, knotted together into something that wants, very badly, to be heard.
The Warden\'s clock-face cracks — its hands spin all the way back!
Time thickens like honey around you.
"NOON." Every bell in Evernoon rings at once.
Mercy lets down her hood. "You will not take her. You will not take ANY of them." She sings the Vespersong.
A single soft bell begins to toll, counting someone down...
"Rest now." A lullaby — and under it, the bells of Evernoon begin to swing...
"—IT!" A hundred mouths finish the sentence at once.
It begins to forget its own shape. Light pours through the gaps — light no longer heals it!
A puppet tears loose from its body and staggers forward!
src/data/content/ch11.js: Your father\'s cutlass, from the wreck of the Gull\'s Return. Still sharp. He oiled it every Sunday.
A brass signal lamp with Lanternfall\'s sigil, found lashed to your father\'s boat with a Keeper\'s knot.
A dented brass censer packed with bitterleaf. Mirefen healers burned it against rot.
A seed that burns without being consumed. Thorns remember fire.
A Dawnguard signet. It opens the Grand Lantern\'s tower.
Crayon on sailcloth, from the children of Kiteholm. Mostly capital letters.
A rusty kitchen knife. Tilly says it is the legendary Lucky Shiv. Tilly is very sure.
Captain Hal Merrow\'s log. The last page is addressed to someone.
It swims through the glass dunes the way an eel swims through weed. The dunes are in the sky now. It has not noticed.
A memory of water seen by someone dying of thirst.
Blindfolded and singing one note. Tamsin\'s acolytes sang the Dawnsong with their eyes covered, so they would hear it better.
Its shell is fused desert glass. Hit it hard enough and it rings.
What remains of Keeper Tamsin: a choir of blindfolded voices singing so loudly they cannot hear the world end.
One voice of many. It sings harmony to a song no one else can hear.
The monks of Frosthollow kept a silent vigil. Some of them are still keeping it.
It hunts by the sound of chattering teeth.
The avalanche that killed Brother Halvard, gathered up and given a grudge.
A slope of snow that remembers falling.
Brother Halvard, kneeling in the snow, apologizing to a mountain. He has been at it for a year.
Mirefen\'s healers used leeches. The leeches have started using the healers.
Lives in the stilts. Bites the ankles of anyone who stands still too long.
It waits under the boardwalks for the rot to finish its work.
Mother Osk, who nursed her village through the rot and could not stop when they died. She is still nursing.
It cries like a feverish child. Do not listen too closely.
An oak that was old when Aurenne was a village. It is very tired of standing.
More thorn than dog, now. It still wags.
Drawn to the last light in any room. Drinks it.
Verdance\'s fairies were said to live as long as a summer. Summer ended.
Elowen, the oldest Keeper, who would not fade. She drank the forest to stay in bloom.
Stormcrown\'s riders flew drakes like these. The drakes kept flying.
It dives with the lightning, never before it.
Vasha\'s honor guard. The armor stands its watch with nothing inside.
A spark that got lost on the way down and decided to stay.
Ardent Vasha, who gave the Hierophant her light because he asked so kindly. She is still announcing his coming.
Cassian\'s chosen. They took the Vesper oath: to hold the moment, whatever it costs.
The last of Garrick\'s men. They stayed because he stayed.
They sing the Vespersong in rounds, to keep the moment warm.
A bell from the City of Bells, given legs and told to toll for the end of time.
Garrick\'s second. He has polished the same breastplate every morning for a year, because no one told him to stop.
Head of the Dawnguard and Cassian\'s sword. He has seen the world broken, and would rather it frozen.
No title now. No soldiers. Just a man with a sword, and another man with a sword.
He is bleeding. So is Bram. Neither of them is sitting down.
Something that happened here, once, on an ordinary day. It wants to happen again.
Lanternfall\'s gulls were always bold. They are bolder dead.
Everything the sea took from Lanternfall, wound together and come home.
It has circled the Lantern for a year. It has never once thought of leaving.
You fought it on the night Sable washed ashore. It remembers you. You were so much smaller.
A little of the light she could not let go of.
Ysolde Halloway, Keeper of Lanternfall, still holding the last light so her daughter can reach the boat.
It walked the sea floor its whole life. The floor is in the sky now. It keeps walking.
It drifts above the reef, pulsing like a slow heart.
It nests in the ribs of drowned ships.
The storm that took Edrin Halloway, remembered by the sea it happened in.
A fever that broke, a year too late.
Clean sheets. Folded corners. Something still lying in them.
Every long night on every ward, given a voice. It sounds exactly like Ilse on her worst day.
Every knight who ever stood the vigil here left a little of themselves in the stone. It stands up to see if you are worthy.
The squires who failed the vigil. They are not angry. Only cold.
The thing Bram saw on the night of his trial. It was never in the hall. It was in him.
Somebody\'s stove, somebody\'s fence and somebody\'s grandmother\'s mangle, walking.
It is a crate. It is a crate with teeth. Do not open the crate with teeth.
It steals buttons, rings, buckles and, given the chance, eyes.
Queen of Scrapfall, the best thief in the sky. Until about five minutes ago.
The Stormwall\'s heart. It has eaten twelve airships. It would like a thirteenth.
The Kingfisher\'s crew never left their guns. Nobody told them the battle was over.
Someone nobody remembers anymore. It does not remember either.
The Gloam, when it tries to be someone.
Every forgotten thing the Gloam ever kept, wanting one more thing to keep.
A star that came too close, to see what all the fuss was about.
The Choir opens a hundred mouths. Other voices answer from the glass.
"I can hear your heart, little thief. It is beating much too fast."
The Choir draws one long breath together...
Frost climbs his robes like a second skin.
"I should have said it the first day. Four words. _This fork is wrong._"
The air goes still. Even your heartbeat waits its turn.
"Where are my little ones? Come back to Mother!"
"Hush, hush. Mother\'s here. Nobody dies in Mirefen."
She draws her brood close, and swells.
The petals turn toward you, slowly, like a face toward the sun.
"Sleep, children. I remember summers that lasted a hundred years."
"HEAR ME! THE NOON IS COMING!" The storm breaks over you.
The storm crowns her. Lightning hangs in the air, waiting. (3/3)
"I gave it to him. I gave it to him. I _gave_ it—"
Garrick lifts his greatsword overhead and waits for an opening.
Garrick sets his feet. "Freeze, boy. You always do."
"Come inside, little bird. It\'s getting dark."
She holds the moment. She has been holding it for a year.
The Lantern flares behind her. The whole room turns gold.
The lamp gathers itself, the way it did every dusk for two hundred years...
The sky-water draws back, the way the sea did on the night of the storm...
"Bed rest. Doctor\'s orders. You look exhausted."
"Night shift. Everyone up. Nobody sleeps on my ward."
It looks at you, and your hands stop working.
The Dread rises over Bram. _You will freeze again._
The Squall King swallows the lightning. The deck hums under your feet...
"You are made of us. Come home. Be no one again."
The Fallen Star burns whiter. Every shadow in the room points away from it...
It flickers, and for a moment you can see right through it to the dark.
The Glass Steps. A choir sings in the dead Lantern. (Danger: Lv 58)
Brother Halvard\'s monastery, frozen to the peak. (Danger: Lv 60)
Elowen\'s forest, withering from the crown down. (Danger: Lv 63)
Ardent Vasha\'s aerie, inside a storm that never ends. (Danger: Lv 65)
The Cathedral of Dawn. Garrick holds it for Cassian. (Danger: Lv 67)
The only Lantern in the world still burning. (Danger: Lv 69)
A brass observatory on a rock that wandered off. Someone is still home.
The sea floor, risen. Every ship the sea ever took. (Danger: Lv 66)
Where Kiteholm\'s rubbish goes. Something lives on it. (Danger: Lv 60)
Where Dawnguard squires stood their last night before knighthood. (Danger: Lv 63)
src/data/content/ch12.js: The same atlas Cassian gave you — new, here. On the flyleaf, in a boy\'s careful hand: "For Lysa, who wants to know where the sun goes."
A cheap festival token, stamped with a sunburst. Someone has scratched "COME HOME SAFE — MUM" on the back.
A length of gold ribbon from the haberdasher\'s stall. It has never frayed.
STR/DEF +14. Immune to Stun and Slow. He said he had a spare. He didn\'t.
MAG/RES +22. Immune to Silence. Warm, still, from his hands.
HP/MP +12%. Halves light and fire damage. A crown of a single afternoon.
SPD +10, critical rate +15%. Immune to Slow, Stun and Doom. A clock hand that will never turn again.
The Drowned Hound had a litter. Forty years in the Gloam, and they grew up.
A festival-goer who wandered too far from the party. Its smile is painted on. So is its face.
Rubble from the broken sun, still warm, still trying to be something.
It is singing a song someone forgot the words to.
Its paper lantern has been lit for forty years and has never burned down.
Bright paper, falling. It has been falling since before you were born.
A Dawnguard as a twelve-year-old remembered them: tall, shining, and never once afraid.
A painted carousel beast. It goes round and round. It has never stopped.
A present nobody ever opened. It resents that.
The kite a boy flew on the last good afternoon. In the memory, it never comes down.
The bell that should have rung one o\'clock. It has been holding its breath ever since.
The festival\'s leading dancer, painted in noon. She has been mid-twirl for forty years and she is very tired.
Someone nobody remembers anymore. It is trying very hard to remember itself.
The night the Lantern failed, the dark came up through the gutters like floodwater.
The feeling of being looked at from the dark, given a shape.
It came up out of the gutters with the others. It is looking for a girl.
The Gloam, the one night it came into Aurenne. It took one child. It has been hungry ever since.
It sings Cassian\'s hymns. It does not know any others.
Plate forged from noon. Inside, nobody — only the idea of someone who would never let you get hurt.
Tick. Tick. Tick. It is counting something. It will not say what.
He has never once raised his voice. He is not raising it now.
Acolytes he remembers. They remember nothing but the hymns.
Cassian and the broken sun, sung into one shape. The king of a single afternoon.
One of the seven pieces. It circles the King like a moth around a— well.
The Vespersong, grown a face. A clock that ate the sun. It does not want anything except for this to never end.
Slow. Inevitable. It has been coming toward you since the moment you were born.
Quick. Restless. Never where it was a moment ago.
I don\'t want to hurt you, Wren. I never have. Please — let me show you.
Sing with me, children. Just once more.
Look at it, Wren. The sun, whole — for as long as I can hold it.
A hand falls still. Vesper\'s face is open!
Vesper\'s hands spin backwards. Every clock in Evernoon begins to unwind — its weaknesses turn with it!
"STAY," says every clock at once. Vesper rewinds itself — but dawn-colored cracks are showing through!
The last toll sounds. Someone\'s time is running out.
A hand reassembles itself out of the ticking.
Vesper begins to hum a lullaby. Stay. Stay. Stay...
The clock-sun swells. It is about to strike noon forever...
Where Cassian\'s frozen afternoon stood. Only a quiet morning now, and two names on a stone.

A small acorn, warm as a held hand. "The key to my secret place."
Thorne\'s Writ
"The girl is to be detained and conveyed to the Cathedral of Dawn. Unharmed." Sealed in black wax.
Marit\'s Ring
MAG +4, RES +4, MP +10%. Inscribed inside: "Keep the light."
Pell\'s Horseshoe
LCK +10, DEF +4. The third horseshoe from over the Pell farmhouse door.
Cliff Kite
Rides the Gale like a thrown knife. Nests in the cliffs and resents everyone below them.
A crab that took one look at the Gale and grew a boulder on its back.
Spume Jelly
Sea-foam that learned to hold a grudge. Spits salt in your eyes.
Thorne\'s Own
The Lord-Commander\'s personal guard. Black trim, a sun with a closed eye, and orders they will not explain.
Mourning Moth
They drink tears. In the Whisperwold they never go thirsty.
Hollow Sapling
A young tree with a hollow where its heart should be. Something whispers in the hollow.
Lost Shade
It is saying something. It has been saying it for a hundred years. It no longer knows to whom.
The Hollow Mother
The oldest tree in the Whisperwold. She gathered the voices of the dead into her hollow so that none of them would ever be forgotten — or ever be allowed to end.
Old Strawman
Three generations of Pells built him. One sack of cheap purple stuffing woke him up.
Bandit Bruiser
Red Tam hires by the pound.
Tam\'s Mastiff
Answers to "Biscuit." Do not call it Biscuit.
Quarry stone that soaked up the violet seam beneath it, and got up.
Bethan, the Crestless Sage
Mender, Arcanist, Ranger, Cantor, Pugilist. "Same old woman. Different tools."
"Stay... stay... STAY."
Her bark splits wide open. A hundred voices weep at once!
"Come back to me, little ones..."
The Hollow Mother draws every voice in the wold into her branches...
Old Strawman bursts into violet flame!
Old Strawman flaps its sleeves. Crows pour out of its coat!
Violet dust gathers in Old Strawman\'s stitched grin...
Port Gale
The Gale Coast
Harbor town of the Gale Coast. Sailors, smugglers, and the Salt & Lantern.
The Whisperwold
An ancient forest where the trees speak with the voices of the dead.
The Heartland
A farming village of beehives and autumn fields. Home of the Crestless Sage.
src/data/content/ch3.js: A bronze bell-hammer worn smooth by forty years of noons. Its name, scratched on the handle, is GLORIA.
A loose page from the Chronicle of the Long Night. Someone has inked over certain words. Thoroughly.
A large ginger cat, currently being carried by Sable. He is tolerating this.
Immune to Sleep and Silence. Beeswax, forty years of bells, and a little spite.
DEF +5, RES +5, HP +5%. Sir Aldous Venn\'s ring. Too big for any finger but his.
RES +5, Afterglow gain +15%. A handbell from the first carillon of Aurenne. It rings true.
The great bell tolls through bone.
The Gloam pulls at the edges of you.
The rooks of St. Aurel\'s have heard the bells every hour of their lives. It has not improved their mood.
Carved to spit rainwater off the roofs. Something down in the drains taught it to spit other things.
Grew fat on what the city flushes away. Is not grateful.
It drinks until it is round, then keeps drinking out of habit.
Lives on the Choir\'s candle-ends. Its dust smells like a cathedral and puts you to sleep like a sermon.
All bone and appetite. It still wags, which is worse.
Aurenne\'s old city watch. Still guarding the gate. The gate is gone.
A candle lit for the dead, forty years ago. Nobody blew it out.
A Sister of Small Mercies. She sings the Dawnsong. Something is wrong with the way she sings it.
Mercy gave it a memory to hold. It dropped it.
Several people, once. Mercy\'s notes call it "an economy of scale."
Wooden rules, first to yield. Nobody has ever told a squire that wooden swords still hurt.
The bell-founders of old Aurenne were buried beside their furnace. One of them got up to finish a job.
The City of Bells. Seat of the Choir, home of the Grand Lantern.
src/data/content/ch4a.js:
s Kindling) and the
// Greyspine Mountains (Frosthollow, Brother Halvard, Garrick
Lift-glass from the Glass Caverns. It hums when you hold it to the sun — and when you hold it near the tuning forks.
The Dawnsong in Brother Halvard\'s cramped hand. One note is circled twice. Beside it: REFLECTION?
An iron key, warm from Halvard\'s hand.
The color of the dunes at noon. You find out it is there when it finds out you are.
A sand wyrm hatchling: the length of a man and all appetite. Its mother is never far.
A shimmer of heat that decided to stay. Drinks fire. Fears the dark.
It is patient. In the Sunscar, patience always eats.
Takes your water first. Then your boots. Then, if you complain, you.
Throws sand, stones and insults, all with remarkable accuracy.
It wears the shape of what you want most. Up close it is only heat and hunger.
A sand wyrm in its prime: forty feet of hunger that swims the dunes like open sea.
Raider-king of the southern dunes. Laughs like a jackal. Fights like three of them.
Its shell is saltglass. It chimes when it walks, which is the only mercy it offers.
Wings thin enough to throw rainbows. It throws them in your eyes.
The caverns grow them like geodes. Nobody knows what wakes them. Something does.
Spins its webs from molten sand. They set like glass, and so do you.
The Queen\'s children. Half-grown and wholly furious.
She has eaten caravans whole. Her scales are saltglass; her song is the sound of the desert breaking.
Hunts in the white. Its coat is snow; its breath is the cold that comes after.
They sing travelers to sleep in the snow. The snow does the rest.
A winter that learned to walk. It does not hate you. It only wishes you were still.
Sleeps under the snow for months. Wakes up hungry and offended.
Old as the monastery, the monks say. Every squire who ever kept the Vigil has heard it howl.
Hangs from the ceiling like an icicle. Falls like one too, but with teeth.
Gray cloaks over Dawnguard steel. They used to guard the dawn. Now they guard something else.
Crossbows wound with Choir prayers. The bolts still hurt.
They hum the same few notes over and over. After a while, you catch yourself humming them too.
Garrick\'s chosen. They do not speak. They do not retreat.
Lord-Commander of the Dawnguard and the Hierophant\'s sword. Nobody has ever asked him to explain himself.
The sand ERUPTS beneath your feet!
Sandmaw shrieks. Something small and hungry answers from under the dunes!
Sandmaw dives beneath the sand... the dune begins to tremble.
"Ha! Lads — fresh meat, fresh water! GET IN HERE!"
Sarn kicks up a wall of sand!
The Queen bursts up through the glass floor!
The Queen SHRIEKS. The cavern walls crack — and the glass comes down like rain!
The Queen calls, and the walls answer with small hungry voices.
The Queen sinks into the sand. The glass floor starts to hum...
The Queen sings. Your armor sings back — and cracks.
Whitefang throws back its head and HOWLS. Snow shivers on the slopes above...
Form up. Shields high. This will not take long.
Still shaking, Kestrel? Aldous would be so proud.
s Lantern. The caravans gather here.
The snow monastery, where the oldest Dawnsong is carved in ice.
src/data/content/ch4b.js: The Pilgrim Road
Moss that grew where a shrine-lamp burned for two hundred years. Still faintly warm. Glows when crushed.
Weepcap Lily
A white bog-lily that has never seen the sun. It weeps a clear sap that smells of rain.
The black heart of Mawmire. The sickness, made solid. Ilse handles it with tongs.
Tarnished Ring
A plain copper wedding ring, found in the Drowned Chapel. Engraved: _T. — always the long way home._
Clover Crown
A crown of clover, pressed flat and brown forty years ago. Lysa Lorne made it for Elowen. Sable keeps it now.
Storm Core
A fist of saltglass that has swallowed a lightning strike. It buzzes against your teeth.
Aram\'s Logbook
A sky-pilot\'s waterlogged logbook, found in the Undercradle. The last page is addressed to someone called Kesi.
Osk\'s Reed Knot
Immune to Poison and Blind. RES +4. Mirefen reed and silver wire; smells of peat smoke.
Pilot\'s Goggles
Immune to Blind. SPD +4, evasion +4%. Aram\'s spare pair; the strap still smells of wind.
Black Bile
A flood of rot-water.
Root Quake
Deep Drink
Lance of the Dawn
The Eye Opens
Bog Leech
Fat with other people\'s blood. Thin with its own patience.
Rot Toad
Mirefen children used to race the toads. Nobody races these.
Swamp-light. Follow it and you will find exactly what it wants you to find.
Marsh Crawler
Mud on the outside. Mud on the inside. A shell like a church door in between.
The Gloam-rot, grown a body. Its spores are the sickness in the village.
The Drowned
Mirefen buries its dead in the water. Since the light went out, the water has been giving them back.
Bog Lurker
The ferrymen call it "the log that moves." They do not call it anything to its face.
Rot Polyp
A bud of Mawmire. It wants to grow up to be just like its mother.
Where the Lantern\'s light used to touch the water, something grew in the dark to fill the space. It is mostly mouth.
Dawnguard Trooper
The Dawnguard swore to guard the light. These ones are guarding the Lord-Commander\'s temper.
Dawnguard Crossbow
Trained to hit a sparrow at sixty paces. Has never once been asked why.
The Thornwood\'s youngest guardians. They have forgotten what they were guarding.
Mossback Boar
So old that moss grows on it. So angry that nothing else does.
Lost Lantern
A spark of the Thornwood\'s Lantern, left behind when its stone was taken. It is looking for the way home.
Bark Mantis
It prays. You do not want to know to what.
Gloam Moth
Drawn to light. There is none left in the Thornwood, so it has started making do with you.
Weaves its webs from thorns. Silk has never occurred to it.
A root that got tired of being underneath things.
Warden of the Thornwood for six hundred years. Its Keeper\'s light went out, and it has been fighting the dark ever since — and everything else that moves.
Storm Cell
A thundercloud the size of a dog, and about as loyal.
Gale Harpy
Rides the Stormcrown\'s updrafts and screams at airships out of professional habit.
Crag Golem
Lightning hit this rock so many times it got up to complain.
Cloud Eel
It swims through cloud the way fish swim through water, and it is just as surprised to see you.
Storm Drake
Born in the Stormcrown, raised on lightning, and fond of airships the way cats are fond of birds.
Keel Sentinel
A watchman of brass and saltglass, set under Skyreach by its first Keepers. It has been watching for so long it forgot who it was watching for.
Dawnguard Lancer
Garrick\'s chosen. They polish their armor twice a day and their consciences never.
Captain Corder
Captain of the Lord-Commander\'s Sunspears. Was in Bram\'s squire class. Has never let him forget it.
The Thunderhead
The Stormcrown\'s eye. For three hundred years Skyreach\'s Lantern held it down beneath the isle. The Lantern went dark, and the storm remembered it was alive.
Mawmire sinks into the black water. The bog itself seems to harden around it.
Mawmire\'s flank splits like rotten fruit. Something small and wet climbs out.
Mawmire drinks the bog. Its belly swells black. _Brace!_
The Warden does not see you. It sees only the dark it has been fighting for a year.
Hollowbark drives its roots into the earth. Briars claw up out of the soil!
Hollowbark drinks from the deep roots. Old sap closes its wounds.
Hollowbark\'s bark splits open, bristling with thorns as long as swords...
"Sunspears! Shields together!"
"Remember this, Kestrel? Stand still. You\'re good at that."
Corder levels his lance...
"Hold the line! For the Lord-Commander!"
The Thunderhead tears loose pieces of itself. They crackle into shape.
The clouds peel back. At the heart of the storm, an eye opens — and looks at you.
The wind falls silent. Your ears pop. The pressure is dropping...
Fern\'s Forage & Fletching
The Windward Exchange
The Fens
A stilt village over the fens. Mother Osk keeps its Lantern — kept it.
The oldest forest in Solmere, and Rootholm at its edge. Elowen, the oldest Keeper, lives at its heart.
The Stormcrown
The rain-lashed foot of the Stormcrown, where the Halcyon waits on her cradle.
Above the Stormcrown
A floating isle of airship folk, riding the storm. Ardent Vasha keeps its Lantern.

s brew for the night before every hard thing.
Ysolde\'s Bread
Restores 800 HP. Dense, a little burnt. Not as good as Nana\'s.
Duskwater Jelly
The tide pools of Lanternfall started glowing at night a week ago. This is why.
Gloamshell Crab
Its shell has gone the color of a bruise, and it rings like crystal when struck.
Drowned Fisher
Lanternfall has given men to the sea for four hundred years. The tide caves remember every one of them.
Tide Wraith
A cold shape that drifts above the pools, humming a lullaby nobody has sung in a hundred years.
Gloam Eel
The eels Ilse once complained about, changed. It is hard to say they are worse. They are certainly purpler.
Shardwing Bat
Its wings have grown crystal edges. It sounds like wind chimes when it dives at you.
Vesper Knight
Lord-Commander Thorne\'s own guard. They do not ask why. That is why he chose them.
The first things to come through after the sky broke. Dogs made of dusk, with embers where their eyes should be.
Falling Ember
A fleck of the broken sun. It burns because it does not know how to do anything else.
The Tidemourner
Everything the sea ever took from Lanternfall, knotted together and wearing itself like a coat. It speaks in a voice you know.
Lord-Commander Garrick
Head of the Dawnguard and the Hierophant\'s sword. He has never once lost a duel, and has never once enjoyed winning one.
The Tidemourner brings the whole drowned sea down on you!
"...help us... it\'s so cold... help..." Hands claw up out of the water.
It calls again, in voices you almost know.
The Tidemourner draws in a long, wet, rattling breath...
It sings, in a man\'s voice, a song about a gull.
"Dawnguard! To me! Show these children what discipline looks like!"
Garrick lifts his greatsword high over his head. "Iron Verdict—"
Marlow\'s Goods

, desc, icon:
s Soup
Restores 700 HP and cures Poison and Burn. Ash-potato. It is always ash-potato.
Letter: "To Mama"
Water-stained. "To Mama, at Port Gale. From Jory." For the Lost Wall in Keelhaven.
Letter: "To Aldo"
Folded small, in a careful round hand. "To Aldo Brannock." For the Lost Wall in Keelhaven.
Letter: "To Teo"
Choir paper, sealed with candle-wax. "To my brother Teo, in Kiteholm." For the Lost Wall in Keelhaven.
Letter: "Dear Sun"
A child\'s writing, in crayon. "DEAR SUN." For the Lost Wall in Keelhaven.
The Sunward Atlas
Cassian\'s gift, swollen with damp. "For Wren, who asks the best questions. — C." You don\'t know why you kept it.
Choir Silk
White silk from the Gilded Psalm\'s banner, with a gold sunburst. For Pell\'s kite.
Glassback\'s Core
A fist-sized heart of living glass, still warm. Proof for Warden Hale\'s bounty.
The Lidless Eye
A cold violet orb. Do not look at it. It is looking at you. Proof for Warden Hale\'s bounty.
Fennick\'s Sailcloth Coat
Light armor. Max HP +8%. Three old sails and a Dawnguard cloak, terribly stitched. It keeps the ash off.
Ash Wraith
Ash that remembers being a person. It drifts toward warmth, and does not understand why the warm things scream.
Cinder Moth
Born in the embers that rained down after the sun broke. It is always flying toward the nearest fire, including yours.
Gloam Hound
The Gloam came up through the cracks in the world, and some of it came up hungry, and shaped like dogs.
Hollow Sailor
Still at its post on a ship that has no sea. It will defend the deck until the end of the world. Which is a problem, now.
Shard Golem
When the sea fell upward it left glass behind — miles of it — and some of the glass got up and walked.
It spins its webs between floating islands. Nobody knows what it catches up there. Nobody wants to.
Skybrine Eel
A sea eel, swimming through the air as if it never noticed the water leave. Perhaps it hasn\'t.
Sun-Ember Wisp
A fleck of the broken sun, still burning a year later. It is warm. Nothing else in the world is warm anymore.
Abyss Eye
The abyss under the islands is not empty. Sometimes it looks up.
Wreck Mimic
A sea-chest from some drowned rich man\'s cabin. It has learned that people will walk straight up to a sea-chest.
Old Fennick
Edrin Halloway\'s fishing partner. The light said Vanguard. He said "fish." The light didn\'t argue.
The Ashmaw
A hound of packed ash the size of a cart. It has been eating Fennick\'s chickens all winter.
The biggest thing the glass ever made. It is so clear you can see the sky through it — bent, and broken, and beautiful.
The Lidless
It has no lid. It has never blinked. It has seen everything that has fallen past its perch for a year.
Brinefang, Unmoored
The serpent of the strait, still swimming the sea that isn\'t there. The Gloam got into it on the way up. It has a scar on its jaw shaped like a Dawnguard shield.
Brine Wisp
A skin of old brine, shed by the Unmoored. It swims on without it.
"Here it comes — GUARD, girl!"
"Let\'s see what\'s left in that arm."
Fennick plants his feet and draws his harpoon back. "Watch my shoulders. When they drop like this — that\'s your cue."
"Hff. I used to be faster. Your father was faster still."
The Ashmaw pounces!
The Ashmaw howls. The ash on the bridge pulls itself up into a smaller hound.
The Ashmaw crouches low, ash streaming off its back like smoke...
Glassback brings its whole weight down on the quarry floor!
Its glass hide clouds over and thickens.
Glassback rears up. Light splinters through its body...
The Lidless looks at you. All of it looks at you.
It blinks — it has no lid, and it blinks — and now there are more eyes.
The Lidless opens wider... and wider...
Brinefang brings the hanging sea crashing down!
Brinefang sheds a skin of brine — and the skin gets up and swims.
Brinefang climbs into the broken sky — higher — higher — and turns, and falls toward you...
Brinefang draws the upside-down sea into its throat...
Gus\'s Salvage & Sundries
Fennick\'s Shard
The Drift
A broken piece of Lanternfall\'s north cliffs. An old man, a burnt soup, two cairns.
The Shattered Sea
A refugee town built from upturned boats. Six hundred people, one soup kettle.
The Strait That Was
The old strait between Lanternfall and the mainland. No water in it now — only wreckage and the long drop.
src/data/content/ch7.js: The Mender of Ash
Ward Water
A bucket from the rationed well, for the Ember Ward.
Sunsalt Phials
The Choir\'s remedy for Gloam-rot. Each phial glows like a coal kept under ash.
Three Tin Tags
DORAN. MAGS. LITTLE COBB. The third sunsalt team.
Captain Buttons
A rag doll with one button eye. Very brave.
Dawnmoss Seeds
Gold-green spores in a Choir apothecary tin. They will grow in anything.
Bell Clapper
The clapper of the Bellwrights\' Tenor. Heavy as a promise, dented from the fall.
Dead Letters
Three letters from Petra\'s bag, posted the day before the world ended.
A Letter for Wren
"My dear restless heart — I have kept a place for you." Choir seal, broken.
Undercroft rats that ate what the rot left behind, and caught it. Their bite carries it on.
Rot Bloom
Gloam-rot, given time and darkness and nothing else to do, learns to flower.
Drowned Acolyte
An acolyte of the Under-Choir. It drowned singing. It is still singing.
Knell Wisp
The last note of a bell that broke mid-toll. It drifts, still ringing, looking for the rest of itself.
Ossuary Warden
Aurenne\'s honored dead were buried with their swords. Some of them never put the swords down.
The Unfinished
One of Sister Mercy\'s Remembrances, never finished. It is trying very hard to remember a face. Any face.
Cistern Eel
They came up the drains when the sea fell into the sky. They are not going back.
Bellshell Crab
It wears a handbell for a shell. When it is angry, which is always, it rings.
Drowned Cantor
A cantor of the Under-Choir. Its voice holds the others together, the way a nail holds a coffin.
Drowned Chorister
One voice in the Drowned Choir. Alone, it is only a drowned child. Together, they are a hymn.
Drowned Precentor
The Under-Choir\'s Precentor. He was told to hold the note until noon. He is a very obedient man.
Old Clapper
A rust-red wyrm that nested in the Reliquary and swallowed a bell whole. It tolls when it breathes.
The Held Note breaks over you — the Dawnsong, sung backward!
The harmony falters. The Precentor\'s note cracks into a wail.
"Louder. LOUDER. Let the water carry it!" The cistern surges.
"Hold it... hold it until noon..."
The Precentor lifts his baton. A drowned voice answers from the water.
The choristers hold one swelling note. Silence one of them — quickly!
_BONNNG._ The sound comes out as fire.
Old Clapper thrashes. Rust and bell-metal rain from the ceiling!
Deep in Old Clapper\'s belly, something begins to toll. Brace yourselves!
Ruins of Aurenne
The City of Bells
The City of Bells, silent and drifting. Ilse\'s Ember Ward keeps its people breathing.
src/data/content/ch8.js: An iron key from the Vigil\'s captain\'s chair, stamped BRIG.
"Children remember the best days best. Evernoon has need of them." Signed with a weeping mask.
A patched blue kite with a painted grin, rescued from a shrike nest.
SPD +4, evasion +6%. The tail of the first kite Pip ever built. Lucky. That\'s science.
Max HP +5%. Dented Dawnguard steel, redeemed from the Baron. Heavy as an apology.
DEF +12, RES +8, max HP +8%. Sir Aldous Venn\'s ring, left behind when the armor emptied. "Good lad."
They nest under the shards and steal anything shiny, blue, or belonging to Wick.
It lives upside-down on the underside of the world and does not understand why you are falling over.
Salvage that wandered off on its own. Its belly is full of airship cogs. Nobody knows why. Gaffer Quill has theories.
When the sea fell into the sky, some of the eels decided the sky was just more sea.
A Vesper soldier. Living, for now. He believes he is collecting the children for their own good. So did every kidnapper ever.
They sing the lullabies. They mean every word.
Armor with a dead man in it — or the memory of one. Evernoon lends them out. They remember their own swords.
A stray note from the Lullaby Engine, still humming. It would very much like you to lie down.
A music box the size of a chapel. It keeps children dreaming their best day, forever. The pins on its drum are tiny teeth.
A knight in black armor and a weeping mask, who holds his blade high in the old Venn Guard. Under the mask is a face Bram knows.
A war-boar with an iron jaw bolted on. It was a gift. It has not forgiven anyone.
The left twin. Says nothing. Hits hard. Fixes Sprocket.
The right twin. Not to be confused with the Kite. The Kite is much scarier.
Former Dawnguard sergeant. "Same job, better hours." Still salutes her opponents before she flattens them.
Undefeated champion of the Scrap Arena. It was a chick when the world ended. It has been growing ever since, out of spite.
s key begins to wind... _tick... tick... tick..._
The Venn Guard falls — one perfect, merciless stroke.
A crack runs down the weeping mask. "Squires. To me." Empty armor answers.
The Penitent lifts his blade high over his shoulder — the Venn Guard. Someone is about to be cut in half. Guard!
The Gale Roc folds its wings and comes down like a falling bell!
The Roc screams. Shrikes pour in from the rafters!
The Gale Roc climbs toward the arena roof...
A shanty town of kites and scrap on a windy cliff-shard. Pip\'s Kites keep watch.
src/data/content/ch9.js:
s Roost, the Boneyard, the wreck of the Benediction, the Cinderdeep.

s key to the lift down to the Boneyard. Greasy, and proud of it.
Stamped in violet ink: ADMIT BEARERS. DO NOT DIE ON MY PROPERTY.
A brass carriage clock from the Benediction. It stopped at seven minutes past the end of the world.
LCK +12, critical rate +8%. Ferro swears it isn\'t marked.
SPD +4, immune to Blind. Too big. You\'ll grow.
s debt collectors. They are polite right up to the moment they are not.
Trained to find anyone who owes the Ledger money. It is never bored.
Rats that learned to eat rust. Their bite turns your blood a funny color.
Hull plate, rivets and a grudge. The Foreman builds them out of whatever falls.
The last spark of a dead engine, still looking for something to turn.
Collects shiny things from the wrecks. Considers your eyes shiny.
Scrappers who went too deep and decided the wrecks belonged to them now.
A rivet gun that learned to fly. The Foreman bolts them together in a hurry.
Something in the Boneyard wanted to fly again, and built itself out of every ship that couldn\'t.
The Gilded Gull\'s strongbox. It has been hungry for a very long time.
They were flying in to hear the Vespersong. They are still singing along.
Rides the Squall the way gulls rode the sea. Screams like one, too.
Spins its webs in the shrouds. Most of what it catches is lightning.
A jelly of rainwater that drifts through the Squall, swallowing lightning.
The galleon\'s Choir guard. It still stands its watch, a year after the watch ended.
A storm drake that nested in the Benediction\'s mainsail and fed on a year of lightning and hymns.
Burrows through rock that has gone soft with heat. Smells of toast.
Molten rock with a sun-ember for a heart. It does not like to be cooled.
Its wings glow from inside. In the Cinderdeep, the lights that move are never lanterns.
Slag that cooled in the shape of a miner. It still swings a pick.
Lives in the lava seams. Comes out to sun itself on the sun.
A worm that found a piece of the broken sun and decided to live inside it.
The Choir\'s sky marines. They were the Dawnguard once. Some of them still believe it.
Knight-Captain of the Steadfast. She lost an eye in the battle Corvin ran from, and has never forgiven him.
The Foreman empties its furnace across the yard!
Gears shriek. The Foreman overclocks — its plating glows red-hot!
The Foreman bolts together a Rivet Drone from loose scrap!
THUNDERHEAD! Lightning walks the whole deck!
Squallmaw tears into the eye of the storm. Frost slides off its crackling hide — but the wind tears at its wings!
Squallmaw drinks the lightning. The deck begins to hum...
The Sunworm opens its throat — the light pours out!
The Sunworm swallows the heart-ember. Its scales blaze white — ice hisses away to steam! But the glare cracks its armour along the seams...
Light gathers behind the Sunworm\'s scales, brighter and brighter...
Slag bubbles up from the floor and takes shape!
"Dawnguard — BREAK THEM!" Severine drives her lance through the whole line!
Severine sets her lance and plants her feet...
A smugglers\' canyon in a fallen mountain. The Halcyon\'s grave — or her cradle.
Where the airships fell when the sky broke.
A pilgrim galleon pinned in a storm that would not end.
Odessa\'s sun-ember mine. The only warm place left in the world.
src/data/content/colosseum.js:

;

// The champion
Bellring Laurel
STR +10, MAG +10, Afterglow gain +15%. Valka wore it for nine years. It still smells faintly of victory and oil.
Sand Hound
Bred under the east stand. They have only ever known sand, crowds and the bell, and they love all three.
Kell the Net
Throws a net, then apologizes. The older brother. Says the net does most of the work.
Kell the Fist
Does not throw a net. Does not apologize. The younger brother.
A war-boar who has eaten three gates and, allegedly, a herald. The herald disputes this.
Glass Scorpion
Shipped from the Sunscar in padded crates marked FRAGILE. The crates were for the handlers.
Bellring Squire
Squires who failed the Dawnguard trials fight here instead. The crowd is kinder than the Lord-Commander.
Sereno the Swift
Fastest blade in the Heartland, slowest to pay his tab. He will steal your purse mid-bout and return it after, with a bow.
The Iron Bull
Cast in the bell foundries from a cracked bell and a bad idea. Hit it right and it still rings.
Mire Lurker
Dredged from the Fens at tremendous personal risk. Ottavio paid the dredgers in tickets.
Mask of Dawn
She prays before every bout and after every win. She has prayed a lot.
Mask of Dusk
He curses before every bout. Nobody has ever heard what he says. Nobody wants to.
The Scythe Matron
Mother of a thousand, mercy for none. The Bellring keeps her eggs in a vault. Nobody volunteers for vault duty.
Storm Kite
They roost in the bell tower and ride its echoes. When the bell rings, they come down to see who rang it.
Phalanx Guard
Three shields, one wall, no gaps. They have drilled together for twenty years and still argue about who stands left.
Valka the Undefeated
Forty-one bouts, forty-one wins. A Skylancer from the north who came to Aurenne for the Dawnguard and stayed for the crowd.
Grizzlemaw thunders across the sand!
Grizzlemaw squeals and tosses its head. The crowd loves it.
Grizzlemaw paws the sand and lowers its tusks... Guard!
The Iron Bull brings its whole weight down — BONG.
Rivets groan. The Iron Bull braces, plates grinding shut.
The Iron Bull rears up on its hind legs, iron screaming... Guard!
The Matron sweeps both scythes through the whole ring!
The Matron shrieks. Her wings blur.
The Scythe Matron raises both scythes high... Guard!
Sunsteel Lance! The whole ring rings like a struck bell.
"Now it is a fight." Valka throws off her cape.
Valka plants her feet and draws the lance back to her ear. Guard!
The Bellring
The Heartland
Aurenne\'s colosseum, east of the bell foundries. Four cups, one champion, and a crowd that bets on everything.

Umbral Hound
Not a hound. The rumor of one — the feeling of being followed home, given teeth.
Murk Ooze
Every spilled thought pools somewhere. Down here, it pools into this.
The Forgotten
Memories nobody kept. They whisper names at you, hoping one of them is theirs.
Drawn to light. There is no light down here, so it is drawn to you.
The Umbral Hound, after it caught up with someone.
Nightmare Weave
Every bad dream ever woken from, knotted together. It wants to finish them.
Eye of Below
It has been looking up for a long time, waiting for something to fall.
Gloamcrystal Golem
Gloam that sat still long enough to crystallize, then got up again.
Ossuary Legionary
A soldier of a city whose name fell out of every book at once. Still on patrol.
Rubble Warden
A town gate that forgot it was a gate and remembered only that it was supposed to keep people out.
Ashen Lamplighter
It still lights the lamps on its street every evening. There is no street.
Carrion Herald
It carried the news of the city\'s fall to no one. It is still looking for someone to tell.
Faceless Saint
A saint whose miracle nobody wrote down. The statue lost its face out of sheer politeness.
Cinder Drake
It burned the archive. It does not remember why, which is the only funny thing about it.
Knight of No Banner
Sworn to a lord nobody remembers, against an enemy nobody remembers, forever.
Archive Creeper
It spins its webs out of unread pages. You can read a sentence or two in them, if you get close. Don\'t.
The very first winter had wolves in it. Nobody was alive to remember them. They noticed.
The light off snow on a morning no one saw.
Glacier Sentinel
Slow as a glacier. Exactly as slow. It is very proud of this.
Snowmelt Serpent
The first thaw. It has been waiting for spring since before there were seasons.
Icebound Vigil
It froze at its post. It is still at its post. Some promises are just weather.
Eye of the Long Winter
Watching the snow fall. Has never once blinked. Would like to.
Its wingbeats are the reason snow drifts. It is not sorry.
The Thing in the Ice
Frozen mid-reach. It thawed just enough to finish the motion.
A shape the world started, and then forgot to finish. It is trying to finish itself out of you.
Noonless Seraph
Light, before anyone decided what light was for.
Primordial Ooze
Everything was this, once. It would like everything to be this again. It is patient.
Sketch of a Beast
Four legs, roughly. A head, approximately. The idea of an animal, charging.
Firstborn Hound
The first animal the sun ever shone on. Every hound since is a copy of a copy of it.
Edge Knight
Where the light ended and the dark began, someone had to stand guard. This is the line, wearing armor.
The Unblinking
The first thing that ever saw anything. It has not looked away since.
First Tree
Before forests, there was one tree. It was very lonely. It has not forgiven anyone for the others.
Wishing Mote
Somebody\'s wish, still looking for them. Swords pass right through it. Spells do not.
Hoarder Mimic
It ate a treasure chest, then everything the chest\'s owner ever lost. It is mostly stomach now.
The Unremembered Knight
Every soldier nobody remembers ends up here. Together, they make one knight. It has a great many names and can say none of them.
The Rime Sovereign
Queen of the first winter. She ruled a kingdom of snow with no one in it, and she ruled it very well.
The First Dark
What everything was before the sun gave it edges. Not evil. Not anything. It would like you to be nothing too, very gently.
Shard of Before
A piece of the First Dark that broke off to look at you more closely.
Lysa\'s Echo
Lysa Lorne, ten years old, hiding since the night of the festival. Nobody ever found her. She is very, very good at this game.
Festival Lantern
A paper lantern from the summer festival, forty years ago. Still lit. Still warm.
The Drowned Hound, Remembered
The first monster you ever fought, the way you remember it: bigger.
Remembered Pup
Even the pups came back bigger.
Brinefang, Twice-Told
Every sailor who survived the strait told the story again. Each time, the serpent grew a little.
Red Tam, Legend (Self-Proclaimed)
Red Tam as Red Tam tells it: eight feet tall, undefeated, beloved by all. The Gloam took him at his word.
Tall-Tale Bandit
Tam says there were forty of them. There were four. These are the forty.
Sister Mercy, as Remembered
Her hymns, her certainty, her gentle voice. The Gloam remembered all of it and none of the doubt.
Gloam Beast, Remembered
It used to be a person. In the memory, it still is, a little.
Glasswyrm Echo
A sand wyrm of the Sunscar, remembered by everyone who ever heard the dunes hum.
Glass Scorpion
Clear as a window. You can see what it ate.
The Penitent, Remembered
The black knight, the hollow mask. The Gloam remembers the armor. It does not remember who was inside.
Garrick Thorne, Remembered
The Lord-Commander, exactly as hard as you remember. Possibly harder. Memory is not a fair judge.
Dawnguard Echo
A soldier who followed orders. The Gloam kept the orders and lost the soldier.
Echo of the Blind Choir
A Remnant\'s hymn, sung back by the dark. Every note correct. None of them meant.
Echo of the Mire Mother
The swamp\'s mother, remembered as she was at the end: sick, and still feeding everyone.
Echo of the Storm Herald
Lightning remembers where it struck. It would like to strike there again.
The Noon King, Remembered
A frozen noon, wearing a crown. It shone so brightly you could not see the man inside it, which was the point.
You, as the Gloam would keep you: sixteen, furious, and on the dock with the Dawnstone in your hand.
Ilse, as the Gloam would keep her: always tending to others, never once asking for anything.
Bram, as the Gloam would keep him: frozen in the middle of his knighting trial, forever.
Sable, as the Gloam would keep her: a nameless girl with someone else\'s face.
The Knight sets its shield. (Iron Stance: steel glances off — lightning and light will not.)
The Knight throws its shield away and grips the greatsword in both hands. (Fury Stance: open to steel, shrugging off spells.)
The First Dark pulls itself into the shape of a wolf — too many legs, too many teeth. (Fire and steel could find its edges.)
The First Dark becomes a winter: long, white and silent. (Fire and lightning could crack it.)
The First Dark wears the shape of a sun. It is the wrong color. (Light feeds it now — shadow and ice will cut.)
The First Dark folds into the shape of a Lantern and sings the Dawnsong backwards. (Wind and blunt force could topple it.)
"...Form up. FORM UP." Bones rise from the rubble to answer.
The Knight lifts its greatsword high. Behind it, a thousand faint soldiers lift theirs. (Guard!)
The Sovereign calls her court. A hoarlight drifts down from the ceiling.
The Sovereign sheds her crown of ice! Underneath, she is all wind and old snow. (Lightning no longer bites — try wind.)
"MY COURT. ATTEND ME."
The air goes still. Frost crawls up your boots, your knees, your breath... (Absolute Zero is coming.)
"...hush." The Dark Before.
"...you have so many shapes. let me try one on."
"...i will unmake you gently. the way a tide unmakes a footprint." Pieces of before break away and drift toward you.
More of it breaks loose. It is coming apart to reach you.
"...it was so quiet, before you. i was never lonely. i did not even have the word."
Everything goes white. The First Dark draws in all the light there is. (Guard. Shell. Now.)
The First Dark breathes in. The light in the room leans toward it... (Brace — the Dark Before is coming.)
"...a HUNDRED! Ready or not, here I come!"
"Twenty... twenty-one... no peeking!"
"Fifty-five... fifty-six... I can hear you breathing!"
"Ninety-eight... ninety-nine..."
"I\'m tired. Is the game over? ...Did I win?"
Lysa covers her eyes. "One... two... three..." (She is counting to a hundred. Get ready.)
"Don\'t go home yet. Please? Everyone always goes home."
"Lanterns! Come play!" Paper lanterns from the festival drift down around her.
Lysa giggles and ducks behind a lantern. (Hidden: blades will miss. Spells will not.)
The Hound howls. The shadows of its shadows answer.
Brinefang drinks the whole remembered sea... (A wave is coming.)
"All forty of you — GET THEM!"
"Rise, child. Your suffering is not over yet."
Sister Mercy folds her hands. "Hush now..." The whole arena goes quiet. (A hymn is coming.)
The Glasswyrm dives into the sand. The arena floor begins to hum. (Brace yourselves.)
The mask cracks. Behind it there is no one at all.
The Penitent kneels and lowers its head, as if in prayer. (It is not praying.)
"Dawnguard! Hold the line!"
"Stay. Stay exactly as you are."
The Noon King raises one hand. It becomes very, very bright. (High Noon is coming.)
"Why did you leave the island? Why did you give him the stone? Why, why, why—"
"Don\'t worry about me. Nobody ever does. That\'s fine. That\'s FINE."
"I can\'t move. I can\'t move. Sir Aldous, I can\'t—"
"Which name is mine? Tell me which name is mine."

Tome. MP costs -15%. Every page is blank until you need it.

Staff. Healing +25%. The Ashen Lamplighter\'s pole, finally put to use.

Robe headgear. Immune to Silence. The Rime Sovereign wore it for a kingdom of no one.

A baby sea serpent. It bit you. You let it.
Aurenne\'s canal carp. They gather when the bells ring.
Fishermen say it hums lullabies under the ice.

Gold scales that stay warm long after dark.

Old Gnarlhide goes down like a felled oak, and the field is quiet.
The Wold Widow
the heart of the Whisperwold
In the Whisperwold\'s heart there\'s a web strung between two oaks, wide as a sail. Whatever spun it is called the Widow, and her brood comes with her.
A web between two oaks, wide as a sail, beaded with dew and worse. Something the color of a bruise sits at its center. It has far too many eyes, and all of them open.
The Widow curls up like a burnt leaf. Her web sags and tears in the wind.
Mother Knot
the sewers under Aurenne
The rat-catchers won\'t go into the deep sewers under Aurenne anymore. They say there\'s a rat king down there, a hundred rats knotted at the tail, and it eats its own young to heal.
A heap in the dark that squeaks with a hundred voices: rats knotted tail to tail into one great shuddering thing. The middle of it has a face.
Mother Knot comes apart into a hundred fleeing rats. None of them look back.
the deep dunes of the Sunscar
Pilgrims crossing the Sunscar talk of a basilisk with one eye of clear glass. Look into it and your legs turn to stone, they say. Look away and it breathes fire.
A long, low drake basks on a dune of fused sand. One of its eyes is clear glass with the sun burning in it. The air around it shimmers.
Glasseye\'s glass eye cracks across. Then the light goes out of it.
Old Belcher
the Drownmere in the Mirefen
In the Drownmere there\'s a toad as big as a cottage. The marsh-folk call him Old Belcher. He sings people to sleep, then sits on them.
What looked like a mossy hillock in the bog opens two yellow eyes. It is a toad, as big as a cottage. Its throat swells like a bellows.
Old Belcher deflates with one long, last croak that echoes across the whole mere.
the ash of the Drift
Out on the Drift there\'s a drake that swims through the ash like a fish through water. Salvagers call it Cinderjaw. The ash catches fire wherever it surfaces.
The ash heaves and something surfaces: a drake of black slag, embers glowing between its scales. Its jaws drip fire.
Cinderjaw sinks back into the ash and does not surface again. The embers go gray.
the Drowned Choir under ruined Aurenne
Under the ruins of Aurenne, where the Choir used to sing, an eel as long as a nave has learned the hymns. Those who hear it stop being able to speak.
In the flooded choir loft, an eel as long as the nave coils between the pews. When it opens its mouth, it sings in a choirboy\'s voice.
Hymnal\'s last note breaks off in the middle. The loft is silent for the first time in a year.
The Scrap King
the Boneyard below Corvin\'s Roost
In the Boneyard under Corvin\'s Roost, the scrap has crowned itself a king: a golem that bolts drones together out of junk, then eats them to mend itself.
A throne of wrecked engines, and on it a giant of scrap wearing a crown of bent rivets. Little drones buzz around it like flies. It stands up.
The Scrap King comes apart bolt by bolt. The crown rolls to your feet. It\'s only a cog.
Grandmother Frost
The monks of Frosthollow whisper about Grandmother Frost: a white shape on the pass that sings travelers to sleep in the snow, and the wolves come for them after.
A shape of falling snow in the shape of an old woman, humming. Wolves of white frost sit around her, like grandchildren listening to a story.
Grandmother Frost stops humming. The snow she was made of settles, softly, over nothing.
the Gloam Rift
Deep in the Gloam Rift there\'s an eye that has never closed. Whoever it looks at falls asleep, and some of them never wake.
An eye as tall as a door hangs in the dark of the Rift, unblinking. You feel very, very tired.
Neverwake shuts. For the first time, perhaps ever, it sleeps.

The management patches all contenders. The management is not liable for pride.
Ottavio Brass
Prize Clerk
I\'ve seen Valka fight forty-one times.
I\'ve lost money forty-one times. I keep betting against her. It\'s a principle now.
When the bell rings, the whole city stops. Even the Cathedral bells wait for ours.
Don\'t tell the Choir I said that.
The Iron Bull was cast from a cracked bell. If you hit it right, it still rings.
Nobody has hit it right.
Kell the Net and Kell the Fist are brothers. Kell the Third sells the pies.
The pies are the most dangerous thing here.
Arena Medic
Between rounds we give you back a quarter of your strength. Any more and Mr. Brass says it isn\'t sport.
Lose a cup and we patch everything. Free. It\'s the only free thing in Aurenne.
src/data/maps/ch10_evernoon.js: Aurenne, forty years ago
Hollis the Baker
Honey-buns! Fresh from the oven! Still warm — they\'re always still warm!
Same pitch. Same breath in the same place.
Honey-buns! Fresh from the— fresh from the— Still warm. Still warm. Still warm.
Look how high it goes! Mama, look! Look how high it goes!
There isn\'t a kite. He\'s holding nothing.
Wim\'s Mother
Yes, love. Very high.
She\'s not looking at him. She\'s looking at the wrong bit of sky. Forty years, the wrong bit of sky.
The Bandleader
And-a-one, and-a-two, and-a—
Play it! Just *play* it!
And-a-one, and-a-two, and-a-one, and-a-two, and-a-one, and-a-two, and-a—
_(her bow hovers a hair above the strings, trembling, waiting for the count)_
Old Bess
Keeper Lorne
The Lantern\'s humming oddly. I\'ll look at it after the festival. There\'s always time after the festival.
He doesn\'t know. He\'ll never know. He\'ll never get to tonight.
Lantern Acolyte
The Keeper says it\'s probably the heat. Probably the heat. It\'s a very hot day.
Little Girl
You\'re the Gloam! You have to catch us before the sun goes down!
Little Boy
But the sun never goes down! Ha ha! The sun never goes down!
Don\'t laugh like that. Don\'t— just don\'t.
Madame Sorrel
Your future, dear? Oh — there isn\'t one. Isn\'t that wonderful?
She looked at me. She actually *looked* at me.
You\'re not from today, are you. Sister Mercy knows you\'re here. She knew before you did.
Young Squire
Some day I\'ll be a knight. A real one. The kind that doesn\'t run.
That\'s him. That\'s Sir Aldous. He\'s— he\'s younger than *me*.
You will be. You were. You were the best one.
_(quietly)_ And you ran, once. Back for me. That\'s the only running you ever did.
Mrs. Lorne
Have you seen my Lysa? She was just here. She\'s wearing her festival dress — white and gold, with a ribbon.
Have you seen my— have you seen— she was just here. She was just here. She was just here.
Cheerful Man
Lovely day for it!
For *what*, friend?
Lovely day for— lovely day for— lovely day for—
Festival Guard
Welcome to the Festival of the Long Light. Enjoy the day.
Enjoy the day. Enjoy the day. Enjoy the day.
The fountain. Its water arcs up and hangs at the top of the arc, glittering, and does not come down.
Trays of honey-buns, glazed and golden. They are warm. They have been warm for forty years.
Nobody has ever eaten one.
The Cathedral doors are painted on. There is no inside. He never went in that day.
The Grand Lantern, humming oddly in the heat. Its light is the color of honey. It will fail tonight. It never gets to.
A cherry tree in full bloom. Petals fall from it constantly, turning in the air — and never land.
The river doesn\'t flow. It glitters in place, every ripple exactly where it was.
The Keeper\'s House
The vanity. A hairbrush with long black hairs in it, and a jar of ribbons, white and gold.
Lysa\'s bed. Under the pillow, a list in a child\'s hand: THINGS TO DO WHEN I AM GROWN UP. The list is very long.
Picture books. One is open to a drawing of an animal with a glossy black coat. Under it, in careful letters: SABLE.
A shelf of paper stars, each with a wish written inside. Most of them are about fireworks.
src/data/maps/ch10_spire.js: The Noon Spire
The Greatest Shard
You came out. Nobody comes out.
No. Don\'t tell me. I\'ve decided I\'m going home.
My boy is in there. Tam. He was nine.
The Choir says when the Hierophant\'s work is done the gate will open, and I\'ll see him at the festival. I\'ve been waiting since the spring.
Is it still spring? I\'ve lost count. Nothing changes up here. That\'s the point, they say.
Old Gideon
Eleven months I\'ve sat here. My Marigold is inside. Forty-one years married.
Some nights I can hear her laughing, through the wall. Same laugh. Same moment. Over and over.
I tell myself that\'s a comfort.
They say inside it\'s always the best day of your life. Isn\'t that what we all want? Isn\'t that what everyone has ever wanted?
I wanted my patients to get better. "Better" means "different." It means tomorrow.
I am. That\'s how I know I\'m still alive.
You beat the Lift-Warden? He took my slingshot once. Did you get it back? ...No? Well. Still.
The big gate never opens. Don\'t bother knocking; I knocked for a week.
But the white ships bring crates round the east side of the plaza. There\'s a lift. A man with a spear stands by it and says "halt" a lot.
Supply line
The great gate of the Spire is sealed with gold. Carved over it, in letters as tall as Pip:
AND THE GOOD DAY SHALL NOT END.
A statue of the Hierophant, arms open, smiling. Someone has left a child\'s shoe at its feet. Then another. Then hundreds.
A statue of a little girl in a festival dress, holding a ribbon. There is no name on the plinth.
The pilgrims\' fire. Nobody needs it for warmth up here. They keep it lit so there is something that changes.
The lift\'s guarded.
The Spire Halls
Clock-cases, floor to ceiling. Each face is painted with the same summer sky. Each one has stopped at noon.
A clock with a child\'s drawing tucked into its glass: a girl, a boy, a big yellow sun, and the word ALWAYS.
The Noon Gate. Warm air breathes through it, smelling of honey and cut grass.
Not back. Never back. East — the balcony.
Lift shaft\'s full of light! East, sparrow — the balcony!

Corvin\'s books: "Navigation for the Reluctant," "Debts and How to Outlive Them," and a much-read book of children\'s bedtime stories with the price still on it.
Ilse\'s stove. Something is simmering. It smells like home, if home were mostly onions.

src/data/maps/ch11_remnants.js: The Glass Steps
THE KEEPER\'S HOURS\nThe sun wakes in the east. At noon it stands above us. At evening it goes home to the west.\nRing the hours as the sun walks them, and the Lantern will hear you.
Glass wall
A wall of glass has grown across the bridge, clear as still water and hard as a vow. Something in the garden below must open it.

A nomad\'s water barrel. On the lid, a tally scratched with a knife: one notch for every day. The notches stop on the day the sun broke. Beside them, in a child\'s hand: STILL HERE. STILL HERE. STILL HERE. Then nothing.
A caravan tent, its poles fused into the glass. Inside, a bedroll, a cold teapot and a child\'s sandal. Whoever lived here packed in a hurry and left the important things.
A Choir pilgrim, still in her traveling sandals, facing the Lantern. She came all this way to hear the Dawnsong one last time.
The Greyspine
A wall of blue ice seals the stair. Deep inside it, the shadow of a monk\'s hand, pressed flat, as if he had tried to hold the avalanche back.
More ice. Above it, very faintly, a voice reciting the same short prayer over and over.
A cairn of stones. On the top stone, in charcoal that the snow has somehow never touched: HALVARD. A monk\'s prayer-cord is wrapped around it. Someone came back for him.
Through a cracked shutter: a monk\'s cell. A cot, a candle stub, and a table covered in drawings of a tuning fork, each with a single note crossed out.
The refectory. Forty bowls set out on a long table, forty spoons beside them. The soup froze a year ago. No one sat down.
The monastery bell lies split in the snow. It rang the hours on this mountain for six hundred years. Then it rang the avalanche.
The Rotting Lake
The village well. A bucket on a rope. The water at the bottom is perfectly clear: the only clean water in Mirefen. Osk kept it that way to the end.

Through the window of the stilt-house: rows of cots, each one neatly made, each one empty. A chalkboard: NAME / HOUR / MEDICINE, filled in until the chalk ran out, then filled in with charcoal, then with a burnt stick.
A child\'s wooden boat on the windowsill, carved with more love than skill. Painted on the side: FOR MOTHER OSK, WHO MADE ME BETTER.
Osk\'s hut. Herbs hang from every beam. On the door, a list of names in her neat hand, each one crossed out, gently, with a single line.
Carved inside the hollow oak, at a child\'s height: LYSA WAS HERE. Below it, in a careful, very old hand: SO WAS ELOWEN.
A cherry tree, still in blossom. The only living thing in the court. Petals fall and do not land; they hang in the air, as if waiting to be told what to do.
Lightning rod
A ward of raw lightning hangs across the bridge, humming like a hive. Your hair stands on end from three paces away.
A storm-rider of Stormcrown, carved in stone, arm flung up to the sky. The inscription: FLY INTO IT. Someone has added, underneath: BUT MAYBE NOT TODAY.
Another rider, younger, laughing. The sculptor caught a crack in the stone running right across the smile, and kept it.
The Stormcrown Pride, Vasha\'s flagship, broken across the rocks. Her figurehead is the Ardent herself, carved mid-shout, finger pointing at a horizon that isn\'t there.

Vasha\'s flight log, under a stone. Last entry: "Gave the Dawnstone to the Hierophant today. He held my hands and thanked me. I have never been so certain of anything." A week later, written so hard the pen tore the page: "WHAT HAVE I DONE."
The Grand Lantern
Aurenne, the City of Bells
Captain Brask
Halt. ...No, I can\'t remember why I\'m meant to say that either. Go on in. Everyone else is dead or upstairs.
The Bellwright Fountain. Dry for a year. Someone has dropped a single coin in it anyway, very recently, for luck.
A statue of the first Hierophant, arms raised to the sun. Someone has chalked a mustache on him. It is a very good mustache.
A Dawnguard cot, the blanket squared to regulation. Pinned above it: a child\'s drawing of a knight with a very large sword, signed TO DAD.
The Lamp Gallery
The cradle of the Great Lamp of Aurenne. The glass is cracked from rim to base. It was the brightest light in the world for nine hundred years.
The Westmost Isle
The village Hearthstone. Cold, for the first time in anyone\'s memory. Someone has left a bunch of dried sea-lavender on it.
Tobias\'s shack. A note pinned under a stone in his square capitals: BACK SOON. DON\'T TOUCH THE NETS. The nets are still here. Nobody touched them.
Nana Brisa\'s house. Through the window, jars of herbs labeled in tiny exact handwriting. One just says: DO NOT. LET WREN. TOUCH.
Halloway House
Two plates. Two cups. A year of ash on both.
Your bed. Unmade, obviously. Some things survive the end of the world.

Your father\'s books. Sea charts, star charts, and the pirate-queen novel with the last chapter torn out. Tucked in its place, a folded paper in your mother\'s hand: "She ends up happy. Don\'t tell Wren, she\'ll want to read it herself."
Your own books, salt-stiff. The Sunward Atlas is not among them. You took it with you. You remember choosing it over a sweater.
The Lantern of Lanternfall
The great lamp of Lanternfall, dark. Inside the brass, where the Dawnstone used to sleep, nothing at all. It is only a lamp now.
Lantern log
src/data/maps/ch11_rites.js: A smuggler\'s sloop. In the hold, crates stamped PROPERTY OF C. ASHE — DO NOT OPEN. Corvin pretends not to see them.
A cot, made with hospital corners. A child\'s drawing is tucked under the pillow: a big woman in a hood, and the words MOTHER OSK MAKES IT STOP HURTING.
A cot, made with hospital corners. On the blanket, a single dried flower, placed very carefully.
A cairn of gray stones. On the largest, chiseled by someone who was not a mason: SIR ALDOUS VENN. HE STOOD BETWEEN.
A stone knight, sword point-down, head bowed. The plinth reads: DAME ORSOLA OF THE WESTMARCH. SHE WAS AFRAID OF HORSES.
A stone knight with a cracked shield. The plinth reads: SIR TEODOR BRAND. HE WEPT AT EVERY KNIGHTING, INCLUDING HIS OWN.
A stone knight, very young, very serious. The plinth reads: SIR ALDOUS VENN, AGE NINETEEN. Somebody has scratched underneath, much later: STILL AN IDIOT. — G.T.
The Rook Queen\'s nest: a ring of buttons, spoons, bottle caps, a brass doorknob, three wedding rings and, right in the middle, a child-sized empty space shaped like a knife.
A kite with a lopsided sun painted on it, tangled in the junk. A name on the spar in crayon: TILLY. PROPERTY OF. KEEP OFF.
The Kingfisher\'s mainmast, snapped. Her colors still fly from the stump: Dawnguard blue, with a kingfisher stitched over the sunburst by someone who could not sew.
A bow gun, still loaded. The gunner\'s gloves are on the breech, laid down neatly side by side, as if he meant to come back for them.
A small bed with a patchwork quilt. Every patch is a different shade of yellow.
A shelf of wooden animals: a gull, a cat, a lopsided horse. Carved by a twelve-year-old, badly, with enormous care.
A star chart, inked on sailcloth. Half the stars are crossed out. Beside the gaps, in tiny writing: "fell?" "fell." "FELL. Bother."
A copy of The Sunward Atlas, annotated in red ink by its own author. The margins are fuller than the pages.
A shelf of books about the sun. Every one ends with the same chapter title: "And Then It Rose Again."

src/data/maps/ch12_evernoon.js: The Gate of Evernoon
The Noon Spire
Brother Anselm
A statue of the Hierophant as a young man, arms open. The plinth reads: HE WHO KEPT THE LIGHT. Someone has scratched underneath: AND KEPT IT. AND KEPT IT.
A statue of a girl of ten holding a book against her chest. The plinth has no name on it. It doesn\'t need one.
Seven sockets are set into the paving before the arch, each shaped like a jagged piece of something round.
A belfry bell, toppled and cracked. Its clapper has been removed and laid neatly beside it, like a sleeping child.
A Vesper soldier\'s helmet, half-buried in ash. Inside, a folded note: "Mira — if the sun really stops, I\'ll be home for supper forever. Save me a seat." The ink has faded to violet.
A small stone at the foot of the arch. Two names, carved by an unpracticed hand: LYSA LORNE. CASSIAN LORNE. Underneath, smaller: "Now they both know where the sun goes."
Beyond the arch there is only a bright, ordinary morning, and a long way down.
Halcyon\'s staying tied off till this is done, sparrow. No coming back — you said it yourself.
Where Evernoon stood there is only the shard, and the wall, and a quiet morning under the new sun. The golden afternoon is gone. Nobody misses it as much as they thought they would.
The dancer smiles at you. Somewhere, faintly, a clock is ticking.
Aurenne, Forty Summers Ago
Welcome, welcome, to the Festival of Long Light! The longest day of the year!
Lemonade! Fresh lemonade! And... swords, apparently. I don\'t remember stocking swords. I don\'t remember stocking anything.
Funny. Same lemon. I\'ve been squeezing the same lemon all afternoon.
Old Pim
Lovely afternoon. Lovely.
I keep meaning to go home for supper. Mira will have the soup on.
Lovely afternoon.
Two sweethearts lean toward each other. They have been leaning toward each other for forty years.
Just KISS already.
Let them have it, kid. Some moments are worth taking slow.
Forty years is not slow, Corvin. Forty years is a medical condition.
Three balls in the air above the juggler\'s hands. They never come down. They never go up, either.
That\'s the worst thing I\'ve ever seen.
He is holding the first note of the Dawnsong. He has been holding it for forty years. He has not taken a breath.
Did you hear? The Keeper\'s little girl has been asking about the purple lights by the old wall. Such a curious child.
Somebody ought to keep an eye on her tonight.
Auntie Bel
Have you seen Miss Lysa? Her brother\'s looking all over.
Miss Lysa! There you are, love. Your brother\'s been looking all over for you.
I am not her.
Miss Lysa! There you are, love.
Fruit Seller
Apples! Apples that never brown!
I\'d eat one, only then there\'d be one fewer. And I don\'t know how to grow more.
Lucky Sel
Sel\'s been about to win since lunch. Never shows his hand.
Somebody ought to call him. Not me. I\'m comfortable.
Squire Venn
Squire Venn! Eyes front! You\'ll have the Lantern plaza tonight, lad, and the Keeper won\'t want a squire who fidgets.
Tonight. Ha. As if tonight\'s ever coming.
Can\'t ring her. Rope\'s stuck fast.
You don\'t ring at noon, see. You ring at the turning of the hour. And the hour never turns.
Mother Dawe
You\'re it! ...You\'re it! ...You\'re it!
I\'m not it. I\'ve never been it. I\'m never going to be it.
The bell tower. Its great bell hangs at the top of the swing, about to fall back and ring the hour. It has been about to for forty years.
An anvil with a half-forged sword on it, still glowing. The smith\'s hammer hangs in the air just above it.

s Memory
Lysa! LYSA!
She\'s not by the old wall. The lights are all over the plaza now. Please — please hurry.
It\'s so pretty...
Frightened Man
Get indoors! The Lantern\'s guttering — the dark\'s coming up through the drains!
Hush, hush. Keep your eyes shut, sweetheart. If you don\'t look at it, it can\'t see you.
Old Watchman
Forty years I\'ve walked this street, and I\'ve never once seen the Lantern flicker.
It\'s flickering.
A chalk drawing on the flagstones: the sun, with a little door drawn in its side. Underneath, in a child\'s capitals: WHERE DOES IT GO?
A child\'s white shoe, the buckle undone. It is facing the wall, as if whoever wore it walked straight on without it.
Here the old city wall is thinnest. The stones don\'t meet. Through the cracks, violet light, and a sound like the sea a long way down.
Lysa\'s ribbon, on the cobbles. When Sable reaches for it, it isn\'t there. It was never really there.
The Noon Stair
Not yet. Everyone\'s by the fire. One last night first.
Not like this. We should catch our breath first.
The Noon Throne

THE WHISPERWOLD — 1 mile.\nTravelers are advised not to answer the trees.\nBy order of the Thistledown Reeve.
A cairn of sea-smoothed stones. A gull feather has been tucked between two of them, carefully.
A cairn of sea-smoothed stones, stacked with care. Someone built this to last.
